request: Employees pick a request topic from presets the organization curates (VPN, Claude, Question, Other for staff; Access, Other for clients), and the screens say Pending / In progress / Completed / Closed

findings.claim: The catalogue read declares a closed domain for `status` but never says what an out-of-domain value answers, while its sibling parameter `audience` is given both a rule and a case for exactly that situation.

witness.detail: contracts:30 declares the query: 'Query: `audience` (`staff` | `client`; omitted returns both), `status` (`active` default | `archived` | `all`).' The Routes row for that route (contracts:15) lists only '`400` `REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.audienceUnknown`; `404`', and no requirement covers `status`: REQ-02-002 (02-request-topics.md:79) is 'IF a create call or a catalogue read carries an `audience` outside `staff` and `client`, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer `400` with `REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.audienceUnknown`.' TC-02-INT-04 (cases:202) pins the reason: 'The read refuses rather than returning everything, so a typo in a query string cannot look like an empty catalogue.' `GET ...?status=activ` therefore has two implementations the document permits equally: refuse with 400 — for which the Error Messages table carries no export, so it cannot be built from this spec — or fall back to the `active` default, which is the empty-catalogue-from-a-typo outcome TC-02-INT-04 says must not happen.

findings.suggestedFix: State the answer for a `status` outside `active | archived | all` on the catalogue read in one sentence, and if it is a refusal give it its message row and a step in TC-02-INT-04 alongside the `audience` typo.

findings.claim: The ordering control is specified to always move the row past its neighbour, and is simultaneously specified to clamp at 0, which produces the tie the same paragraph rejects as unacceptable.

witness.detail: contracts:354 'up sends the `sortOrder` of the row above minus one ... so the moved row lands strictly past the neighbour it moved over and the list comes back reordered. A value outside `0`-`32767` is clamped to the bound (validation rule 6).' contracts:357 '**Decided:** the moved row takes a value strictly past its neighbour. Rejected: sending the neighbour's own value, which leaves both rows tied on `sortOrder` and the name tiebreak (REQ-02-009) deciding the order, so a press can leave the list exactly as it was.' Inputs: a curator creates a staff topic named `Alpha` with `sortOrder: -5`, which TC-02-INT-03 (cases:187) says is 'stored with `0` and sorts first of all'; the seeded `VPN` at 10 is now the second row. Pressing up on `VPN` sends 0 - 1 = -1, which validation rule 6 (contracts:274) clamps to 0. Both rows now hold 0 and REQ-02-009's name tiebreak puts `Alpha` first: the press left the list exactly as it was — the outcome the Decided note rejects. Known Gaps (02-request-topics.md:308) states the other side of the same mechanism: 'repeated moves into one gap can close it and leave two rows sharing a value, which falls to the name tiebreak.'

findings.suggestedFix: Decide one rule and state it in the Screens section: either the clamp wins and the sentence claiming the list always comes back reordered goes, or the first row's position is reached some other way (a value the screen may not compute from a bound it can hit). Do not leave both claims standing.

findings.claim: What a member without `manage-request-topics` sees at the Request topics address has two readings that build different screens, and the spec never says what is drawn instead.

witness.detail: contracts:412 'Permission-limited (`user`, `viewer`) | The Settings row is not rendered and neither is the page's Add control; the route answers `403` regardless.' — a page that renders with its Add control removed. TC-02-E2E-05 (cases:531) 'The direct navigation renders no topics page and no add control', asserting `request-topics-page` (absent) at cases:534 — no page at all. The Required data-testid table (contracts:291) records `request-topics-page` as 'present' with no absent twin, unlike `request-new-submit` (contracts:315), which carries both. The two readings are materially different and both are consistent with the rest of the spec, since REQ-02-008 (02-request-topics.md:120) lets a `user` read the catalogue with `200`, so a read-only page is buildable. Neither statement says what the address renders when it renders no topics page.

findings.suggestedFix: State once, in the UI Description row, what a caller without the capability gets at that address — nothing drawn, a not-found screen, or a read-only list — and make the testid row and TC-02-E2E-05 say the same thing.

findings.claim: The four words are fixed for the five `Request` statuses, but the vacation section rendered on the same list keeps its own vocabulary and the spec never says whether it changes.

witness.detail: The Status Labels table covers `open`, `answered`, `granted`, `declined`, `cancelled` only, and edge case 9 (02-request-topics.md, Edge Cases) has the same control select vacation rows: 'The vacation rows shown are the rejected and cancelled ones.' `vacationStatusesFor` (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:479) maps the page vocabulary onto `pending | approved | rejected | cancelled`, and the vacation cards draw those stored values (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx, `requests-card-status-${id}`). So selecting Closed can leave a card reading Rejected on the same screen. TC-02-UNIT-05's 'The map has an entry for every stored status, so no status can render as a raw column value' reads wider than the map it describes.

findings.suggestedFix: One line saying the vacation section keeps spec 10's words and why, or that it adopts these.

findings.claim: The seeding case's transaction assertion is settled by a timestamp comparison that neither proves nor disproves what it claims.

witness.detail: cases:159 'The seed rows and the `Organization` row share a creation timestamp from the same transaction.' `createdAt` is `TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260724114549_init/migration.sql:32), so two separate transactions a millisecond apart share the value and pass, while a client-generated `now()` per statement inside one transaction differs and fails a correct implementation. The rest of the case — the seeded rows, their order, `createdByAccountId` null, the second organization's isolation — is observable as written.

findings.suggestedFix: Assert the atomicity the requirement is about — a signup that fails leaves neither the organization nor any topic — or drop the sentence and let REQ-02-015 rest on the rows being there at the first read.

findings.claim: The seeded staff catalogue is nine topics where the request named four.

witness.detail: The request names 'VPN, Claude, Question, Other for staff; Access, Other for clients'. The Seed Data table adds Repository, Environment, Server, Admin panel and Documentation to the staff audience. Every one of them is a row in a table this spec creates rather than a route, a contract change or a new writer of a shipping row, so it does not block — but it is what every new organization starts with, and Known Gaps already reasons about the set as if it were the retired access-kind list.

findings.suggestedFix: Confirm the wider seed was wanted, or cut it to the four the request named and let a curator add the rest.

findings.claim: Two rows of the Asserted column record only the present half of an assertion the cases make both ways.

witness.detail: contracts:291 '`request-topics-page` | Settings > Request topics | present', asserted absent by TC-02-E2E-05 (cases:534). contracts:307 '`request-new-topic` | New request modal | present', asserted absent by TC-02-E2E-06 (cases:547). The table already carries the two-sided form elsewhere — `request-new-submit` (contracts:315) reads 'present, and absent when the picker is empty'.

findings.suggestedFix: Give both rows their absent half, in the same shape as the `request-new-submit` row.

findings.claim: `sortOrder` states an answer for a value out of range and none for a value that is not an integer.

witness.detail: contracts:274 '| 6 | topic `sortOrder` | Optional integer, 0-32767 | ... an out-of-range value is clamped to the bound |'. `sortOrder: "top"` and `sortOrder: 1.5` are neither in range nor out of it, and no message row exists for either; TC-02-INT-03 exercises 40000 and -5 only.

findings.suggestedFix: Say that a non-integer is refused with a named message, or that it is coerced, in the same cell.

findings.claim: This spec turns two body fields that the shipping create route accepts today into a refusal, so every existing caller of POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests changes.

witness.detail: REQ-02-022 (02-request-topics.md:216) answers `400` `REQUEST_MESSAGES.classifierNotAccepted` when the body carries `type` or `accessKind`; the route today validates them together and stores them (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:368, packages/validation/src/requests.ts:133-163), and the new-request modal sends both (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/NewRequestModal.tsx:177). Recorded so the change is confirmed as meant, not because anything upstream needs editing.

findings.suggestedFix: None. Confirm the retirement was intended.
